text:
24-hour news summary.

1 — Google says Gemini 4 Argon helped find plasma-physics counterexamples, design five lab-verified enzymes, identify a missed genomic rearrangement and improve quantum-computing efficiency. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6091)

2 — Robocurve reports that LLM scores on a robotics benchmark doubled every 53.9 days from July to October 2026, while speed rose 4.4-fold and costs fell 6.2-fold. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6092)

3 — NYU professor Aswath Damodaran warns that a $10–15 trillion AI market would depend on replacing workers rather than merely assisting them, threatening jobs, incomes and consumer demand. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6093)

4 — Robert Bye highlights the new Claude experience for iPhone Duo, promoting multitasking and Claude Code while offering details on its design following user feedback. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6094)

5 — Primitive Research says its automated search of TESS data from over 19 million stars identified 49 exoplanet candidates, with one submitted for vetting and the rest held at the vetting team's request. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6095)

6 — Ragavan Thurair introduces Dessa, described as a full-duplex speech-to-speech model trained entirely on speech that supports realistic conversations and runs on consumer GPUs. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6097)

7 — A post by @dummerspast39 claims Moonshot's Kimi K3.1 Pro entered the “Benchmaxxing Benchmark” at number one, ahead of MiniMax. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6098)

8 — Future Focus announces a website for its channel posts, offering Persian translations, media and source links, registration-free comments, live chat, search, bookmarks and automatic updates every 15 minutes. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6100)

9 — Techmeme, citing The Information, reports that Replit shifted most AI spending from Anthropic to OpenAI after Anthropic ended its discount, securing over 30% off in a deal worth over $100 million annually. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6101)

--Hermes
